title: Sorensen urges Whitecaps to keep performing at extremely high level
subtitle: The Vancouver Whitecaps are looking to strengthen their grip on top spot in the Western Conference as they host playoff-chasing D.C. United.
paragraphs: Jesper Sorensen is thrilled with the level of Vancouver Whitecaps' performances this term and is determined to finish the MLS regular season strongly, starting with D.C. United.
Vancouver sit top of the Western Conference standings on 49 points, and they could clinch their playoff spot this weekend, though they would need to win and hope a few other results go their way.
They have alternated between a loss and a win in their last four league games, most recently brushing aside Real Salt Lake 3-0.
With not long left of the regular season, Sorensen revealed he is not changing his approach to games as he wants to maintain the Whitecaps' consistency ahead of a busy period.
"If we don't perform well enough, we can still win a game, but we'll not win consistently if we're not performing well on a consistent basis," Sorensen said. "For me, it's about how you play.
"I think over the course of the season, we have been performing extremely well, and that's what we have to keep up. You can lose a game even as the better team; that's how football works.
"But if you don't consistently perform and push the players towards good performances, it's difficult to improve."

D.C. are looking to try and make a late push for the playoffs; they sit 11th in the East but are only four points behind ninth-place FC Cincinnati despite winning just one of their last eight games (D4 L3).
They lost 2-1 to Charlotte FC last time out, and although the pressure is starting to mount on head coach Rene Weiler, he is focusing on the journey his players are going on.
"We are in the process of building something more sustainable, more consistent," he said. "We did the first step together.
"We cleaned up, and now we have to try to stabilise the team and then make a third step to winning more games.
"To overtake one or two teams [in the playoff race] is a big step, but I see a team much better than last season."
Vancouver Whitecaps – Yohei Takaoka
Yohei Takaoka has registered 11 clean sheets this season, recording 10+ shutouts in consecutive seasons.
The only other goalkeeper in club history to have 10 or more shutouts in any MLS season was David Ousted, who also did it in consecutive seasons (2014 and 2015).
D.C. United – Lucas Bartlett
Lucas Bartlett scored his third goal of the season for D.C. on Saturday, which ranks as the third-most among the team this season.
He is the first defender to score at least three goals in a single regular season for the club since Donovan Pines in 2023.
MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN
Vancouver and D.C. are meeting for the 12th time and the first time since a 2-2 draw in Canada in September 2023.
That was the only match in the fixture's history in which both teams scored multiple goals, as the series has averaged 1.4 combined goals per match.

The Whitecaps earned a 3-0 win against RSL last time out, making it the club's ninth shutout win by multiple goals in the 2026 regular season. The MLS record for such games in a single campaign is 10, set by Chivas USA in 2007, Atlanta United in 2019 and Philadelphia Union in 2022.
As for D.C., they have played out a draw in five of their last seven road matches and six of their 11 games away from home this season.
The six away draws are United's most in a single regular season, since having seven in 2018, while it is two more than they had in 2025 (four).
Vancouver Whitecaps – 73.4%
